This is a highly misleading article.

Whether sugar is 'natural' does not matter at all. What matters is the quantity and the type, and to some degree, how fast it is absorbed. Apart from HFCS all sugar is natural including table sugar, which is just concentrated cane sugar. The only way "natural"comes into it is that natural in situ sugar may come with more fiber etc which is more filling and more slowly absorbed. And a few vitamins perhaps.

You definitely can screw up your metabolism with natural sugar. For example I doubled my cholesterol by eating 12 apples a day for 2 months.

Sugar ain't sugar. In particular fructose, and the fructose component of sucrose (table sugar) and high fructose corn syrup behave very differently than other carbohydrates. Generally fructose cannot be use by any other organ than the liver. Unless the liver is depleted - e.g. by running a marathon - it will be converted into fats, and nasty fats for that matter. So simply put, think of fructose as metabolically a fat.

Whether the fructose comes from apples or HFCS doesn't matter much. It might affect high much you eat, as the fiber in fruits makes you fuller from its sheer bulk. So fruit juice, with no fiber, is more easily fattening than the original fruit, and just as fattening as a coke.

Glycemic index is way out of date and highly misleading. GI and the related Glycemic Load have some value in showing that fast digesting starches for example can spike your blood glucose quite badly, putting a lot of pressure on your pancreas and damaging your body via high blood glucose, which in excess reacts with proteins and damages them.

But, it falsely gives the impression that high fructose foods are good for you, because they have low GI. They have low GI because fructose normally cannot be turned into glucose which is what is measured by GI. Unfortunately fructose is turned into fat usually (see anove) and triggers all sorts of nasty inflammatory reactions, production of LDL cholesterol etc.
